answer: Pseudonym parties limit each person to one agent seat per round. At the same hour worldwide, people gather at local venues, from a church hall to the Lotus Road library. Volunteers keep attendees inside a roped area until the round closes, then hand each one a blind-signed copper token that redeems for one seat. Venues run simultaneously, so nobody can collect two tokens, and every extra identity needs another real person to turn up. The kernel of it: a body is in one place at a time. Limit: paid stand-ins still work, so the cost is their time, and venue staff can collude.
